standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So you're a wise old man, huh?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Less of the 'old' man, if you please!
But yes, I suppose you could say that. I prefer to think of myself as a sage.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So what's a sage doing here?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: I've spent most of my life studying this world in which we live. I've strode through the depths of the deadliest dungeons, roamed the murky jungles of Karamja, meditated on the glories of Saradomin on Entrana,
and read some dusty tomes in the Library of Varrock.
Now I'm not as young as I used to be, I'm settling here where it's peaceful.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has not completed Vampyre Slayer:

steps.npc: It's a pity about that vampyre that keeps attacking the village. At least Saradomin protects me.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: That's quite an exciting life you've had.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Now I'm here, perhaps I could offer you the benefit of my experience and wisdom?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Thanks! So you can help me?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Well, I imagine you've gathered up quite a lot of stuff on your travels. Things you used for quests a long time ago that you don't need now.
If you like, I can look through your bank and see if there's anything you can chuck away.
Alternatively, you can bring items here and show them to me. If I see that it's something you don't need, I'll let you know. I might even be willing to buy it.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So you'll help me clear junk out of my bank?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Yes, that's right. Or I'd be happy to chat with you about the wonders of this world!

options.text: Could I have some free stuff, please?

steps.player: Could I have some free stuff, please?

steps.npc: Deary deary me...

steps.text: If the player is in a F2P world:

steps.npc: I'm not giving out free money, but if you try again later I'd be glad to reward you if you'd do a little job for me.

steps.text: If the player is in a members world:

steps.npc: I'm not giving out free money, but I'd be happy to reward you if you'll do a little job for me.

options.text: Ok, what do you want me to do?

steps.player: Ok, what do you want me to do?

steps.npc: I'm sure I can think of a few little jobs. This won't be a quest, mind you, just a little favour...

options.text: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.player: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.npc: Please do!

steps.text: (See subsequent dialogue section down below)

options.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.npc: I'm sure I can think of a few little jobs. This won't be a quest, mind you, just a little favour...

steps.text: Continues to his tasks

options.text: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.player: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

options.text: Can I get another hood for my Quest Point Cape?

steps.player: Can I get another hood for my Quest Point Cape?

steps.text: The Wise Old Man hands you a free hood.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-dialogue.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.npc: You don't appear to have enough space in your inventory. Come back and see me when you do.

options.text: Can I buy a Quest Point Cape, please?

steps.player: Can I buy a Quest Point Cape, please?

steps.npc: Gladly, though they cost 99,000 coins.

steps.text: The Wise Old Man sells you a Quest Point Cape and a hood to wear with it.
If the player only has one or no inventory space open:

steps.npc: All skillcapes come with a hood - you're not going to be able to hold them now. Try again another time.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have enough coins:

steps.player: I'll have to come back another time.

options.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.text: If the player is in a F2P world:

steps.npc: Thanks, but I don't have anything I need doing right now.

steps.text: If the player is in a members world:
Continues to his tasks

options.text: What did you ask me to do?

steps.text: Continues to his tasks

options.text: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.player: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

options.text: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.player: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.npc: Please do!

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Wilderness, please?

steps.npc: If Entrana is a land dedicated to the glory of Saradomin, the Wilderness is surely the land of Zamorak.
It's a dangerous place, where adventurers such as yourself may attack each other, using all their combat skills in the struggle for survival.
The Wilderness has different levels. In a low level area, you can only fight adventurers whose combat level is close to yours.
But if you venture into the high level areas in the far north, you can be attacked by adventurers who are significantly stronger than you.
Of course, you'd be able to attack considerably weaker people too, so it can be worth the risk.
If you dare to go to the far north-west of the Wilderness, there's a building called the Mage Arena where you can learn to summon the power of Saradomin himself!
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
As you wish. Farewell, [player name].

steps.player: What can you tell me about jungles?

steps.npc: If it's jungle you want, look no further than the southern regions of Karamja.
Once you get south of Brimhaven, the whole island is pretty much covered in exotic trees, creepers and shrubs.
There's a small settlement called Tai Bwo Wannai Village in the middle of the island. It's a funny place; the chieftain's an unfriendly chap and his sons are barking mad.
Honestly, one of them asked me to stuff a dead monkey with seaweed so he could EAT it!

steps.text: If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.npc: Further south you'll find Shilo Village. It's been under attack by terrifying zombies in recent months, if my sources are correct.

steps.text: If the player has completed Shilo Village:

steps.player: I've dealt with them, although there are a few still knocking about.

steps.npc: The jungle's filled with nasty creatures. There are vicious spiders that you can hardly see before they try to bite your legs off, and great big jungle ogres.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Oh, the dwarven realms?
Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.
Still, it's much more friendly now. You can visit the vast dwarven mine if you like; the entrance is on the mountain north of Falador.
If you go further west you may be able to visit the dwarven city of Keldagrim. But they were a bit cautious about letting humans in, last time I asked.

On the other hand, if you go west of Brimhaven, you'll find a huge underground labyrinth full of giants, demons, dogs and dragons to fight. It's even bigger than the caves under Taverley, although the Taverley
dungeon's pretty good for training your combat skills.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What mystical realms can I visit?

steps.npc: Well, you've been to Zanaris. I met a fairy years ago who said she lived there. She was an incredible warrior, considering that she wasn't even a metre tall.
Also, in my research I came across ancient references to some kind of Abyss. Demons from the Abyss have already escaped into this land; Saradomin be thanked that they are very rare!

steps.text: If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

steps.npc: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

steps.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What's the biggest monster in the world?

steps.npc: There's a mighty fire-breathing dragon living underground in the deep Wilderness, known as the King Black Dragon. It's a fearsome beast, with a breath that can poison you, freeze you to the ground or
incinerate you where you stand.
But even more deadly is the Queen of the Kalphites. As if her giant mandibles of death were not enough, she also throws her spines at her foes with deadly force. She can even cast rudimentary spells.
Some dark power must be protecting her, for she can block attacks using prayer just as humans do.
Another beast that's worthy of a special mention is the Shaikahan. It dwells in the eastern reaches of Karamja, and is almost impossible to kill except with specially prepared weapons.

steps.text: If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Actually, that one's dead. I've been helping a barmy hunter who'd sworn to kill it.

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: Poison and how to survive it

steps.npc: Many monsters use poison against their foes. If you get poisoned, you will not feel it at the time, but later you will begin to suffer its effects, and your life will drain slowly from you.
Over time the effects dwindle to nothing, but if you had already been wounded you might die before they wear off completely.
Fortunately, followers of Guthix have devised potions that can cure the poison or even give immunity to it.
Should you wish to use poison against your own enemies and those of our Lord Saradomin, there is a potion that you can smear on your daggers, arrows, spears, javelins and throwing knives.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
As a general rule, tougher monsters drop more valuable items. But even a lowly hobgoblin can drop valuable gems; it just does this extremely rarely.
If you can persuade the Slayer Masters to train you as a Slayer, you will be able to fight certain monsters that drop valuable items far more often.
You might care to invest in an enchanted dragonstone ring. These are said to make a monster drop its most valuable items a little more often.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are these strange monsters that keep appearing out of nowhere and attacking me when I'm training?

steps.npc: Ah, I imagine you see a lot of those.

Creatures such as the rock golem, river troll and tree spirit dwell in places where adventurers frequently go to train their skills. While you're training you will often disturb one by accident. It will then get angry and
attack you. The safest way to deal with them is to run away immediately, but they sometimes drop valuable items if you kill them.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Ha ha ha... There are plenty of heroes. Always have been, always will be, until the fall of the world.

steps.text: If the player has less than 80 quest points:

steps.npc: If you'd do a few more quests, you'd soon become a fairly noted adventurer yourself.

steps.text: If the player has 80 or more quest points:

steps.npc: You're quite a noted adventurer yourself!
But I suppose I could tell you of a couple...

Yes, there was a man called Arrav. No-one knew where he came from, but he was a fearsome fighter, a skillful hunter and a remarkable farmer. He lived in the ancient settlement of Avarrocka, defending it from
goblins, until he went forth in search of some strange artefact long desired by the dreaded Mahjarrat.
Perhaps some day I shall be able to tell you what became of him.

But do not let your head be turned by heroics. Randas was another great man, but he let himself be beguiled into turning to serve Zamorak, and they say he is now a mindless creature deep in the Underground Pass that
leads to Isafdar.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Where did humans learn to use magic?

steps.npc: Ah, that was quite a discovery! It revolutionised our way of life and jolted us into this Fifth Age of the world.

They say a traveller in the north discovered the key, although no records state exactly what he found. From this he was able to summon the magic of the four elements, using magic as a tool and a weapon. He and
his followers learnt how to bind the power into little stones so that others could use it.
in the land south of here they constructed an immense tower where the power could be studied, but followers of Zamorak destroyed it with fire many years ago, and most of the knowledge was lost.

steps.text: If the player hasn't completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.npc: Perhaps one day those lost secrets will be uncovered once more.

steps.text: If the player has completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.npc: I hear you've been very helpful to the wizards who are working on the mysteries of the rune stones.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I suppose you'd know about the history of today's cities?

steps.npc: Yes, there are fairly good records of the formation of the cities from primitive settlements.
In the early part of the Fourth Age, of course, there were no permanent settlements. Tribes wandered the lands, staying where they could until the resources were exhausted.

This changed as people learnt to grow crops and breed animals, and now there are very few of the old nomadic tribes. There's at least one tribe roaming between the Troll Stronghold and Rellekka, though.

steps.text: If the player has completed Mountain Daughter:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them. They're all mad.

steps.npc: Truly, their faith in natural spirits is rather foolish, but they're a pleasant enough people.
Anyway, what was I saying? Ah, yes...
One settlement was Avarrocka, a popular trading centre.
In the west, Ardougne gradually formed under the leadership of the Carnillean family, despite the threat of the Mahjarrat warlord Hazeel who dwelt in that area until his downfall.

steps.text: If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: He'll be back, just you wait!

steps.npc: Oh dear, I hope you haven't done anything rash!

steps.text: If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.npc: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: The Wise Old Man of Draynor Village

steps.player: Tell me about yourself, old man.

steps.npc: Ah, so you want to know about me, eh?
Mmm... what could I say about myself? Let's see what I've done...
I've delved into the dungeon west of Brimhaven and heard the terrifying CRASH of the steel dragons battling each other for territory.
I spent some years on Entrana, where I learnt the techniques of pure meditation.
I've wandered through the vast desert that lies south of Al Kharid and seen the great walls of Menaphos and Sophanem.

steps.text: If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper:

steps.player: That feline statue you've got on your bookshelf there - I'm sure I saw something like that when I was in Sophanem.

steps.npc: I've always liked to collect little trinkets to remind me of the time when my life was more - ah - exciting.

steps.player: So you've spoken to the Sphinx, then?

steps.npc: Spoken to a sphinx, you say? My dear young lady, you can't possibly be serious!
Ha ha ha! The people who live deep in the shifting sands of the desert will often tell travellers tall tales of strange beasts, but that doesn't mean any of it's remotely true!
Please, adventurer, there is nothing to be gained by interfering in matters you do not understand.
Even if such a creature were to exist...
EVEN IF SUCH A CREATURE WERE TO EXIST it would be terribly dangerous for you to get involved in its business.
I have heard of terrible things happening to travellers in that land, and I would not wish for you to be dragged into anything like that.
Indeed, I have heard of adventurers doing the most shameful and blasphemous deeds believing themselves to be acting on behalf of some false god!
So please do not speak to me of this matter again. Now, I believe I was telling you of my adventurous youth...
Apart from all that, I've spent many a happy hour in dusty libraries, searching through ancient scrolls and texts for the wisdom of those who have passed on.
Plus plenty of other adventures, quests, journeys... Is there anything else you'd like to know?

steps.player: I heard that Gielinor has three gods.

steps.npc: Indeed. This is correct: Saradomin, Guthix and Zamorak.
Saradomin, the great and glorious, gives life to this world.
Zamorak craves only death and destruction.
Guthix, calling itself a god of 'balance', holds no allegiance, but simply aids whatever cause suits its shifting purpose.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site:

steps.npc: What did you say?

steps.player: I discovered a buried altar to a god called Zaros.

steps.npc: Please, do not speak further of this. No good can come of meddling in such things.
Adventurer, my patience is limited. Speak to me no further of this - this - this foolishness.

steps.text: If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

steps.npc: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!

steps.text: If the player has completed Temple of Ikov but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: I've heard of another god, called Armadyl.

steps.npc: What is this of which you speak?

steps.player: A strange man asked me to go into the Temple of Ikov and steal the Staff of Armadyl.

steps.npc: And what makes you believe in this 'Armadyl'?

steps.player: Well, there were servants of Armadyl living down in the depths of the temple. They'd been there for generations, guarding the staff.

steps.npc: So you trusted the word of these people who had been sitting down a hole all their lives?
I wouldn't worry about this sacred 'armadyllo' anymore. Just another foolish myth.

steps.text: (If the player with the Guardians of Armadyl:)

steps.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

steps.npc: That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.

steps.text: (If the player sided with Lucien:)

steps.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

steps.npc: YOU'VE DONE WHAT?
Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.

steps.text: If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: How about Tumeken, Elindis, Icthlarin and the Devourer?

steps.npc: What names are these?

steps.player: Down in Sophanem, they've got a chief god named Tumeken, plus a fertility goddess named Elindis. Icthlarin is their god of the dead and the Devourer...

steps.npc: Adventurer, what folly leads you to think any of these - things, exist?

steps.player: But I've met Icthlarin! He'd got a jackal's head!

steps.npc: It is hot in that land, and the heat can affect a traveller in strange ways. Tell me, when you met 'Icthlarin', had you been feeling at all unwell?

steps.player: Well, now you mention it, I'd just been hypnotised by a weird woman I met in the desert.

steps.npc: So a strange woman interfered with your mind, then you met a man with the head of a jackal, and you decided he must be a god?
Well, make sure you don't get hypnotised again, and I'm sure you'll not meet any more jackal-headed men claiming to be gods!
It'd probably be best if you don't go there again.

steps.player: But you've been all around that area, haven't you? When you were travelling?

steps.npc: Indeed, I have.

steps.player: So you'd know all about their gods?

steps.npc: I know what I know.
And knowing what I know, I do not speak of this matter. Perhaps you would be wise to heed my example.

steps.player: I wanna know about the wars of the gods!

steps.npc: Ah, that was a terrible time. The armies of Saradomin fought gloriously against the minions of Zamorak, but many brave warriors and noble cities were overthrown and destroyed utterly.

steps.text: If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.npc: You have visited Uzer, and seen for yourself the damage that could be wrought by an elder-demon in its wrath.
Before the Zamorakian forces could be utterly routed, Lord Saradomin took pity on them and the battle- scarred world, and allowed a truce.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Very little is written about the tribe of the Mahjarrat. They are believed to be from the realm of Freneskae, or Frenaskrae - the spelling in this tongue is only approximate.
One of them, the foul Zamorak, has achieved godhood, although none knows how this came about.
Other Mahjarrat who have been particularly active upon this plane are Hazeel, Lucien, Azzanadra and Zemouregal.

steps.text: If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: Hazeel will rise again, you'll see!

steps.npc: Adventurer, your actions fill me with concern!

steps.text: If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.npc: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.

steps.text: If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl in Temple of Ikov:

steps.npc: Truly, your bravery exceeds your stature. But I fear his defeat will not be permanent.

steps.text: If the player sided with Lucien in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've met Lucien. He paid me very nicely for bringing him a staff he wanted.

steps.npc: Traveller, I beg of you, do not have further dealings with such creatures! You do not know their power as I do.

steps.text: If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Azzanadra taught me some ancient magical powers after I unlocked the pyramid where he had been trapped.

steps.npc: Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.

options.text: Wielding the power of the gods

steps.player: Can I wield the power of Saradomin myself?

steps.text: If the player has completed Mage Arena I:

steps.npc: I see you are already learning to summon the power of Saradomin.

steps.text: If the player hasn't completed Mage Arena I:

steps.npc: If you travel to the Mage Arena in the north-west reaches of the Wilderness, the battle mage Kolodion may be willing to let you learn to summon the power of Saradomin, should you be able to pass his test.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I want to ask you about your hat.

steps.npc: Why, thank you! I rather like it myself.

steps.text: If the player has not yet seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

steps.player: Did you steal it from the bank?

steps.npc: Me? Steal from the bank? Whatever do you mean?

steps.player: There's been a break-in at Draynor Bank, and I bet you did it.

steps.npc: Oh my goodness, what in the world could make you think I did such a thing?

steps.player: Well, you've been sitting here looking at the bank ever since you moved into this house. Now someone's robbed the bank, and suddenly your house is full of expensive stuff!

steps.npc: Oh dear, oh dear...
So what do you think I did? March across the street, smash the bank wall, knock out the bankers and steal all the money?
I'm an old man! I walk with a stick! How could I possibly have done that?

steps.player: So you didn't rob the bank?

steps.npc: Just run along now, be a good lad, and don't worry yourself about me or my finances!

steps.player: Hmmm... But I'll be keeping an eye on you.

steps.npc: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.text: If the player has seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

options.text: You stole it off that woman in the bank!

steps.player: You stole it off that woman in the bank! You stole all this valuable stuff too!

steps.npc: Stole it? How could you possibly think I did such a thing?

steps.player: I saw you robbing the bank! You killed all those people!

steps.npc: Deary me, [player name], your imagination is running wild! What could make you think you saw me do that?

steps.player: I've seen a security recording that shows you robbing the bank. The bank's guard showed it to me.

steps.npc: You've seen the bank's security recording?
Tut tut tut... Oh well, at least you'll never be able to tell the bank about me. They'll never listen.

steps.player: So you're just going to get away with it?

steps.npc: That's my plan, yes.
Wrong? WRONG? I'll tell you what's wrong!
I've spent my whole life travelling the world, doing quests for people, saving lives, saving villages from terrifying monsters and all that sort of thing.
Now I'm old, and where do I have to live? In this freezing old house next to a pig-sty, with a bunch of yobs outside who can't keep their hands off the market stalls! What sort of reward is that?
So don't talk to me about right and wrong!

steps.player: Maybe someone SHOULD talk to you about right and wrong...

steps.npc: Bah!
Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

steps.player: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.npc: You could buy one off another player, or wait until they're next made available by the Council.
Ohhh no, I don't intend to part with this. Would you like to ask me about something else?

options.text: You should give it back, you know.
You should give it back, you know.

steps.player: You should give it back, you know.

steps.npc: No, I think I'll keep it.
Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: That was quite an exciting quest we did together!

steps.npc: Oh yes, it was certainly a fitting end to my adventuring days. Your fight against the Sea Troll Queen was highly impressive!

steps.player: Are you tempted to go on another quest in the future?

steps.npc: No, I feel I am a bit old for that kind of thing now. New times need new heroes, and I'm sure you'll always be there to answer the call!

steps.player: I'll certainly see what I can do!

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: When we finished fighting those sea trolls, you said you'd finished with adventuring, didn't you?

steps.npc: Yes, that's right. I'm an old man, there's no denying it, and I need a nice quiet retirement.
Besides, I think you've proved that the new generation has its own heroes and adventurers - I should step back and let you get on with it!

steps.player: Does this mean you're not going to do any more big robberies?

steps.npc: Well, since you saved my life when we were fighting the Sea Troll Queen, I don't mind telling you... I trust you won't tell anyone about this?
I might just have something in mind. After all, that little bank incident went very smoothly.
I retired from adventuring and questing. The episode in the bank was hardly a quest, more like a shopping trip!

steps.player: Your shopping trip killed 3 bank staff and several innocent bystanders, not to mention the watchman!

steps.npc: I've saved countless villages from unspeakable terrors and slain innumerable evil monsters - surely I deserve some sort of reward in return? Yet what did I get? NOTHING!
You yourself would get pretty angry if you did a long and dangerous quest and didn't get any reward from it, eh? I'm sure you would!
Well imagine how I felt at the end of a long life of questing when was left penniless, and I had to move into this thief-infested village! This little shack was falling apart when I arrived!
You go speak to that hag who keeps looking through my window - she'll show you how it used to look before I could afford to redecorate it!
Being noble and virtuous simply doesn't put food on the table, and I don't intend to sit in banks begging like so many people do these days.

steps.player: So all those quests in the past, when you saved people from monsters and stuff like that... You only helped them because you wanted a reward?

steps.npc: No, it wasn't always like that. I used to be satisfied just knowing that I'd helped, and that was reward enough.

But eventually I realised that people forgot about me as soon as the danger was gone, and I wasn't even getting paid properly for my services. Sometimes they offered training in the various skills, but that's no use to me!
I eventually realised that the only way I could get a proper reward for my life's efforts is if I took the reward myself. So I took up my cape and staff and headed for the bank.

steps.player: And now you're planning to do another robbery? Didn't you get enough from the bank?

steps.npc: Perhaps not... But enough of this matter! Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

using-items-on-wise-old-man.text: If the player has not gone through the initial dialogue first:

steps.npc: Humph! You could at least say hello before waving your items in my face.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-of.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-of.npc: I suppose you could use that in combat.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-on.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-on.npc: I suppose you could use that for defense.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-low-value-ru.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

after-observing-his-telescope.player: I see you've got your telescope pointing at the Wizards' Tower.

after-observing-his-telescope.npc: Oh, do I? Well, why does that interest you?

steps.player: It just seems a bit odd.

steps.npc: Odd? There's nothing odd about a fascination with the magical arts. Besides, the architecture of that Tower is truly remarkable, for one who studies such things.

steps.player: So you're not planning to attack the Tower?

steps.npc: No, I wouldn't dream of doing anything of the sort!

after-observing-his-telescope.text: If the player has seen the bank robbery cutscene:

steps.player: Well, you robbed a bank, and I bet you're now planning something to do with that Tower!

steps.npc: No, no. I'm not planning anything like that again.
Well, this is rather embarrassing, but I think there's some kind of monster in my house. Could you go upstairs and get rid of it, please?

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

options.text: Where do I need to go?

steps.player: Where do I need to go?

steps.npc: I think it's somewhere upstairs. It kept me awake all last night.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Mine some copper ore and tin ore. The furnace in Lumbridge can smelt them into bars of bronze.

steps.npc: I need a few bronze daggers to keep the goblins at bay. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Mine some iron ore. The furnace in Lumbridge can smelt them into bars of iron.

steps.npc: I need some iron arrowheads to put on the arrows I was making. Please bring me [#].

I'd like some chunky iron warhammers. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Just look around the woods south-west of Varrock.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: If you get the tanner in Al Kharid to turn some cowhides into leather, you'll be able to make the cowls yourself. Buy needles & thread from the crafting shop in Al Kharid if you need any.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: There's a pub not far from here that will sell you plenty of that. Go west to Port Sarim.
I don't have a decent larder here, so I can't store food very well. Now I'm out of loaves of bread. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Mix some flour and water to make bread dough, then bake it on a cooking range.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: You can buy shears from the general store east of here. Shear some sheep, then spin the wool into balls on the spinning wheel in Lumbridge Castle.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: If you get the tanner in Al Kharid to turn some cowhides into leather, you'll be able to sew the gloves yourself. Buy a needle & thread from the crafting shop in Al Kharid.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Eggs are usually found where chickens are farmed.
My undergarments are getting a bit worn out. I'll be needing some sheets of silk to patch them. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: There's a man in Al Kharid who sells it very cheaply. If you ever take any to Ardougne you'll get a good profit.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Mine some clay. Then use a container full of water to soften it. In the Barbarian Village you'll be able to form this into pots. Just don't bake them.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Swamp tar is found south-east of here. Add it to a pot of flour and cook it on an open fire to make the paste.

wise-old-man-tasks-delivering-items-to-t.npc: I need some potatoes, if you'd be so kind. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: There's a field of those north of Lumbridge.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Use a knife to chop some logs into arrowshafts. Then add a feather to each arrowshaft.
I need some bronze spears. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: If you kill some of those pesky goblins, you're bound to get some bronze spears.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: You'll find bones easily enough if you fight creatures.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Mine some clay. Then use a container full of water to soften it. In the Barbarian Village you'll be able to form this into pie dishes. Just don't bake them.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: You should find some big rats south-east of here in the swamp.
I need a few lumps of copper ore. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: It should be easy enough for you to mine some copper ore.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

I need a handful of feathers to stick in my beard. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: The cheapest way to get feathers is to kill chickens.
This house is a bit cold, so I could do with some normal logs to burn. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: I suggest you take an axe and chop down some standard trees.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: You could try killing some chickens, then cooking their meat.
My footwear is getting a bit worn out, so I need a few pairs of leather boots. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: If you slaughter some cows, you'll get cowhides easily enough.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: If you pick some flax, you can use the spinning wheel in Lumbridge Castle to spin it into bowstrings.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

I'd like a bit of grain. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: There's a field full of it north of here.
I need a few lumps of tin ore. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: You shouldn't have any trouble mining tin ore.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Use a small fishing net to get [anchovies/shrimps] from the sea south of here. Then cook them on a fire or range.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Use a bucket of sand with some soda ash on a furnace.
